reading.body:
Poolside is a foundation model company whose one disclosed technical result is a 6, 13% training throughput gain on NVIDIA Grace superchips by offloading MLP activations to host memory.

Poolside describes itself as building open-weight foundation models and has released the first two Laguna models, M.1 and XS.2, along with a runtime for training and operating agents. Those models are offered through two product experiences in research preview. The disclosed research is about training efficiency on NVIDIA Grace-based superchips, using NVLink C2C as an alternative to selective activation checkpointing, with negligible memory overhead.

The available facts do not include model sizes, parameter counts, energy use, or any connection to grid or building constraints. No litigation, no MCP servers, and no tracked products appear in the facts held about the company, so the compute footprint beyond this one hardware-specific result is unknown.
